Given system of equations:
$$\begin{aligned}
2x + y - z &= 0 \\
x + y + z &= 9 \\
2x + 5y + 7z &= 52
\end{aligned}$$

Write the augmented matrix $[A|B]$:
$$\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}
2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\
1 & 1 & 1 & 9 \\
2 & 5 & 7 & 52
\end{array}\right]$$

Apply row operations to reduce to row echelon form:

Interchange $R_1$ and $R_2$:
$$\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}
1 & 1 & 1 & 9 \\
2 & 1 & -1 & 0 \\
2 & 5 & 7 & 52
\end{array}\right]$$

Perform $R_2 \to R_2 - 2R_1$ and $R_3 \to R_3 - 2R_1$:
$$\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}
1 & 1 & 1 & 9 \\
0 & -1 & -3 & -18 \\
0 & 3 & 5 & 34
\end{array}\right]$$

Perform $R_3 \to R_3 + 3R_2$:
$$\left[\begin{array}{ccc|c}
1 & 1 & 1 & 9 \\
0 & -1 & -3 & -18 \\
0 & 0 & -4 & -20
\end{array}\right]$$

Since rank of coefficient matrix $A$ equals the rank of augmented matrix $[A|B]$ (both are $3$, equal to the number of variables), the system is **consistent** and has a **unique solution**.

Back substitution:
1. $-4z = -20 \implies z = 5$
2. $-y - 3(5) = -18 \implies -y - 15 = -18 \implies y = 3$
3. $x + 3 + 5 = 9 \implies x = 1$

**Solution:** $x = 1$, $y = 3$, $z = 5$.
proTip: Always check the ranks of matrix A and augmented matrix [A|B] to comment on consistency before solving.
